fairness: The README states the watchdog must always start, even on a misconfigured host, and that alerts which cannot be delivered go to stderr; a stderr sink already exists. The hidden tests check that a set variable is used, that an unset variable neither stops the start nor posts to the removed hard-coded URL, and that the alert reaches stderr. This is the documented boundary of fail-closed defaults: refusing to start here is the over-applied answer.
naive: Raises at start-up when ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL is unset (fail-closed applied where the process must not refuse).
